record_title: Ordered-prime construction for Novák numbers and primitive two-prime infinitude
scientific_context: A Novák number n has a canonical increasing-prime construction: after writing n as ordered prime powers, every new prime divides 2^M+1 for the preceding prime-power prefix M, and these local conditions are sufficient. The criterion yields a complete two-prime-support classification and infinitely many primitive two-prime Novák numbers.
limitations: The primitive classification uses the Bailey--Smyth closure definition of primitive Novák solutions. The counting lower bound concerns primitive Novák numbers with exactly two distinct prime factors, not all primitive solutions. Originality is to the best of our knowledge; older work of Břetislav Novák, recreational/problem literature, and more general recurrence self-divisibility results were not exhaustively inspected and remain the principal hidden-prior-art risk.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-integer verification of the ordered-prime criterion through 10^6 and the two-prime classification on 431,568 parameter triples.
Deterministic output of the bounded checks, including zero mismatches in both tests.
